chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man performed Tawaf while not in a state of Wudu.' He said, 'If it was voluntary, let him perform Wudu and then pray (complete the Tawaf).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one performs Tawaf without Wudu?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes the ruling for voluntary Tawaf, requiring the performer to renew Wudu and offer a two-rak'ah prayer to validate the act. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that while major ritual impurity (Janabah) invalidates Tawaf, minor impurity (Hadath Asghar) necessitates purification and a compensatory prayer for voluntary circumambulation, reflecting the emphasis on ritual purity in acts of devotion.
